correctness.rationale: In kQ/J^2, the commutator at each arrow a:u->v is exactly (c_u-c_v) wedge x_a=0 for the m tuple coordinates. An arbitrary unit (vertex torus plus J radical) conjugates x_a by a scalar t_u/t_v and an additive multiple of c_v-c_u. Therefore when colors differ the arrow value is gauge-removable; when equal it is a free k^m-vector. For any nonzero arrow support F on equal-color endpoints, projective directions contribute P_m=(q^m-1)/(q-1) each and scalar amplitudes modulo incidence torus contribute (q-1)^(|F|-n+k(F)); loops and parallel edges are correctly counted. Summing over q^(mk(F)) constant-on-F colorings yields the exact Tutte/random-cluster evaluation. Top polynomial degree n+beta(G) comes from all nonbridge edges; freely selecting b bridges gives the leading coefficient q^b/(q-1)^(n-k(E)). Infinite distinct q lines reconstruct the bivariate polynomial. Independent five small-case direct full unit-orbit enumerations checked paths, a loop and parallel edges; the proof is valid for all prime powers, though small code used prime q.

value.rationale: A uniform closed form for every commuting tuple length in every finite radical-square-zero quiver algebra is a natural representation-theoretic enumeration and links exact moduli to a standard graph invariant. Nontrivial loop and cycle holonomy effects are captured explicitly; the top-degree term reveals cycle rank, and all parameters determine Z_G, making the theorem structurally informative rather than a routine isolated count.

limitations: Finite quivers, finite fields, J^2=0, ordered commuting m-tuples under algebra-unit conjugacy (not automorphism or quiver-isomorphism orbits).
The finite checker does not sample nonprime finite fields; all-field proof is algebraic and independent of the checker.
Historical possibility of an equivalent quiver gauge-orbit/Tutte identity remains.
